newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia seeks palm oil joint ventures overseas.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia seeks palm oil joint ventures overseas.

text.p: Malaysia is seeking to set up joint ventures to grow palm oil in Africa and Latin America to maintain its leadership in the edible oil sector, Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik said on Monday.

Lim said he would be leading a mission to Mexico, Brazil and Equador in November to explore prospects of cultivating palm oil on a joint venture basis to cater for the U.S. market, the national news agency Bernama quoted him as saying.
Lim, addressing a palm oil congress, said he hoped to make similar visits to African countries for joint ventures to cater for the European market.
Lim said such joint ventures would help overcome the shortage of plantation land and labour in Malaysia as well as enhance Malaysia's position as a big market player.
There were no government restrictions on Malaysians participating in joint ventures to cultivate oil palm in other countries, he said.
Lim also said Malaysia was becoming a major supplier of oleochemicals, in line with its efforts to move downstream.

At present, 15 plants have a total capacity of 800,000 tonnes a year to produce fatty acids and glycol. New ones were being built to produce more sophisticated oleochemicals including esters, Lim said.

About 20 percent of Malaysia's export volume would be products from the oleochemical sector by the turn of the century, double the present level. In value terms, it would amount to almost half the export earnings from the palm oil sector, Lim said.
The area planted with oil palm in Malaysia is projected to increase from 2.52 million hectares at present to 2.9 million hectares by the year 2000, he said.
Malaysia's output of crude palm oil was forecast to reach 8.8 million tonnes by year 2000 compared with 7.8 million tonnes produced last year.
About 90 percent of the palm oil produced last year was exported, generating earnings of $5 billion.
